chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The traveler and the camel-driver who moves about and has no fixed residence completes the prayer and fasts the month of Ramadan."

key_terms.الْمُكَارِي: The traveler or one who travels frequently
key_terms.يُتِمُّ الصَّلَاةَ: Completes the prayer (prays full, not shortened)

ai.seo_question: Do travelers and nomads need to shorten their prayers and skip fasting?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi cites this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to define the specific category of 'Mukari' and 'Jamal'—nomadic traders lacking a fixed domicile. Unlike standard travelers who shorten prayers, this group is obligated to perform full prayers and complete Ramadan fasting, highlighting a distinct legal status based on residential stability rather than mere distance. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the exemption of *Qasr* prayer requires a defined travel context, whereas continuous mobility without a home base maintains the full ritual obligations.
